x: Those that showed surprise last year when Bob Roath chopped our course record down to 1:45:53 were simply astounded on July 16th this year when 21 years old Graham Taylor of Cambridge Harriers re-wrote the record book with a truly outstanding 1:39:47.
After an opening lap of 76 seconds Jim Hogan, the European Marathon Champion, took the lead followed by Graham Taylor, the Polytechnic marathon victor, and the rest of the field.

Graham Taylor, who set a magnificent course record of 1hr.39m.47s. the previous year, was unfortunately prevented from turning out by injury, and with the withdrawal by Peter Yates, the race seemed from the start to lie between Scottish international Jim Wright of Tipton, and Barry Collins of Surrey AC.

Blackheath's Richardson won by a mere couple of strides from Watson (Cambridge H.), both having run fast enough to have been over a quarter of a mile clear of the field in any of the previous 18 races, apart from that of 1966 when Graham Taylor set the remarkable course record of 1:39:37.
